extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers / Scientific Review Group members evaluating grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NIH grant peer reviewers to evaluate the Protections for Human Subjects criterion in applications per 45 CFR 46 and NIH policy, including decision flow (No HS / Exempt / Yes non-exempt), worksheet items, and clinical trial monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant designation of human subjects involvement and required attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must designate if human subjects are involved, and if so, whether the proposed activities meet the criteria for exemption. Applications that involve human subjects must include a Protection of Human Subjects attachment that addresses the required points. Applications that are not proposing human subjects research but will use human data or biological specimens, must provide a justification for the claim of no involvement of human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should check that the designation is present and that the Protection of Human Subjects attachment addresses the required points; if materials/data are used but no human subjects claimed, justification must explain that materials were collected for another purpose AND none of the investigators can readily link materials/data to subject identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer decision flow: No Human Subjects designation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application designates that No Human Subjects are involved, determine whether the research proposes the use of human cells, specimens, or data from living individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NO (no use of cells/specimens/data from living individuals) — rate the Protection of Human Subjects section as Not Applicable. If YES — assess adequacy of justification for non-involvement (materials collected for another purpose AND none of the investigators can readily link materials/data to subject identifiers). If adequate, rate Not Applicable; if inadequate or missing, rate UNACCEPTABLE and EXPLAIN WHY.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer decision flow: Exemption claim adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application designates one or more Human Subjects exemptions, determine whether the claim for exemption is adequately justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If YES (exemption claim adequately justified) — rate the Protection of Human Subjects section as Acceptable. If NO — rate the Protection of Human Subjects section as UNACCEPTABLE and EXPLAIN WHY. Reviewers should check which exemption category is claimed and whether the application meets the listed criteria for that exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer decision flow: Human Subjects = Yes (non-exempt) — address 4 required points
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application designates Yes for Human Subjects without exemption, determine whether the application adequately addresses the four required points in the Protection of Human Subjects attachment. For clinical trials, also consider Data and Safety Monitoring Plan and Board if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the four points are adequately addressed — rate Acceptable (refer to the Worksheet to Assist in Reviewing the Required Points). If not — rate UNACCEPTABLE and EXPLAIN WHY. Reviewers must prepare written comments describing specific concerns unless Not Applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four required points for Protection of Human Subjects (high-level)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that propose to involve human subjects must address the following four points: (1) the risk to subjects; (2) the adequacy of protections against risk; (3) potential benefits of the research to subjects and others; (4) the importance of the knowledge to be gained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four points form the core of the Protections for Human Subjects criterion and are evaluated as part of the Additional Review Criteria. For clinical trials, also include a data and safety monitoring plan and a DSMB for Phase III trials. Reviewers should factor evaluation of protections into the overall scientific merit and impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks to Human Subjects (Worksheet Point 3.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application adequately describe (a) Human Subjects Involvement, Characteristics, and Design, and (b) Study Procedures, Materials, and Potential Risk, including:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should look for: description and justification for proposed involvement of human subjects; subject population(s) and assignment procedures; role of collaborating sites and investigators; description of research interventions and interactions; description of what research material, data, and information will be collected; access to personally identifiable information collected and retained; management and protection of materials and information; source(s) of previously collected materials and links to living individuals; all potential risks to subjects and the level of risk; any alternative treatments or procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Protection Against Risks (Worksheet Point 3.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application adequately describe (a) Informed Consent and Assent, (b) Protections Against Risk, and (c) Vulnerable Populations (if relevant), including:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should look for: process for obtaining and documenting informed consent, parental permission, and assent; waiver justification for any elements of consent; how risks (including privacy and confidentiality) will be minimized; ensuring necessary medical/professional intervention for adverse events; plan for handling incidental findings; and additional protections for vulnerable populations such as pregnant women, fetuses, neonates/children, and prisoners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential Benefits of Proposed Research (Worksheet Point 3.1.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application adequately describe how potential risks to subjects appear reasonable in relation to anticipated benefits to participants and others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should assess the balance of risks and benefits and whether benefits (to participants or to others) justify the risks described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the Knowledge to be Gained (Worksheet Point 3.1.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application adequately describe how potential risks to subjects appear reasonable in relation to the importance of the knowledge that may result from the study?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should consider the societal/scientific value of the knowledge to be gained and weigh that against the risks posed to subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plan / Board for Clinical Trials
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed research includes a clinical trial, the application should describe an appropriate Data and Safety Monitoring Plan that includes: a description of a monitoring plan, who will be responsible for monitoring, and the process by which Adverse Events (AEs) and Unanticipated Problems (UPs) will be reported to all relevant regulatory bodies. A Data and Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) is expected for multi-site clinical trials involving interventions that entail potential risk to participants, and generally for Phase III clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should assess whether the monitoring plan is appropriate to the trial's risk, whether responsibilities and reporting processes are clear, and whether a DSMB is proposed when required by trial phase/scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Research (45 CFR 46.102) — what counts as research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research: A systematic investigation, including research development, testing, and evaluation, designed to develop or contribute to generalizable knowledge. Activities that meet this definition constitute research for purposes of this policy, whether or not they are conducted or supported under a program that is considered research for other purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance lists activities that are NOT research for purposes of this policy (examples: certain scholarly/journalistic activities, public health surveillance, criminal justice agency activities, authorized operational activities for intelligence/homeland security). Reviewers should use this definition to determine whether an activity meets the policy definition of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Human Subjects (45 CFR 46.102(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Human Subjects: A living individual about whom an investigator obtains information or biospecimens through intervention or interaction and uses, studies, or analyzes them; or obtains, uses, studies, analyzes, or generates identifiable private information or identifiable biospecimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions of intervention (physical procedures/manipulations), interaction (communication/interpersonal contact), private information, identifiable private information, and identifiable biospecimens. Reviewers should apply these to decide whether the project involves human subjects as defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Involving Coded Private Information or Biological Specimens — when not human subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that involves only the use of human specimens or data is not considered human subjects research if all subjects are deceased OR the data/specimens were not obtained specifically for the proposed research AND none of the investigators involved can ascertain the identity of the subjects, either directly or indirectly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check whether specimens/data meet these conditions; if not, human subjects protections apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 1 — educational settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Research, conducted in established or commonly accepted educational settings, that specifically involves normal educational practices that are not likely to adversely impact students' opportunity to learn required educational content or the assessment of educators who provide instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes most research on regular and special education instructional strategies and research on the effectiveness/comparison among instructional techniques, curricula, or classroom management methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 2 — surveys, interviews, observation, educational tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that only includes interactions involving educational tests, survey procedures, interview procedures, or observation of public behavior (including recording) if at least one of the following criteria is met: (i) identity cannot readily be ascertained; (ii) disclosure would not reasonably place subjects at risk of criminal/civil liability or be damaging to financial standing, employability, educational advancement, or reputation; or (iii) identity can be ascertained but an IRB conducts a limited review per §46.111(a)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should check recording and identifiability conditions and whether limited IRB review is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 3 — benign behavioral interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Research involving benign behavioral interventions with adults, with prospective agreement to the intervention and information collection, where interventions are brief, harmless, painless, not physically invasive, not likely to have significant adverse lasting impact, and not expected to be offensive or embarrassing. Criteria for identifiability/limited review/disclosure parallel Exemption 2; if deception is used, this exemption is not applicable unless subject authorizes deception via prospective agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include playing online games, solving puzzles under noise conditions, or allocation tasks involving nominal cash. Reviewers should confirm prospective agreement and that interventions meet the 'benign' criteria; deception generally negates this exemption unless the participant authorized being unaware/misled in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 4 — secondary research where consent not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary research uses of identifiable private information or identifiable biospecimens are exempt if at least one of these criteria is met: (i) information/biospecimens are publicly available; (ii) recorded such that identity cannot readily be ascertained and investigator will not contact/re-identify subjects; (iii) research involves use of identifiable health information regulated under 45 CFR parts 160/164 for permitted purposes; or (iv) research conducted by/for a Federal department using government-generated/collected info under specified privacy safeguards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess public availability, identifiability, investigator access to identifiers, and applicable privacy/regulatory protections to determine whether this secondary use qualifies for exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 5 — federal research and demonstration projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and demonstration projects conducted or supported by a Federal department or agency (or subject to approval by agency heads) designed to study, evaluate, improve, or otherwise examine public benefit or service programs, including procedures for obtaining benefits or services, possible program changes, or changes in payment methods/levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each federal department/agency must publish a list of such projects on a publicly accessible site prior to commencing the research. Reviewers should confirm project inclusion on such lists when Category 5 is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 6 — taste and food quality evaluation studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Taste and food quality evaluation and consumer acceptance studies are exempt if wholesome foods without additives are consumed, or if a food is consumed that contains an ingredient at or below a level found to be safe by FDA or other designated agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should check the nature of the food consumed and whether it meets the safety-level criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 7 — storage/maintenance for secondary research (broad consent required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Storage or maintenance of identifiable private information or identifiable biospecimens for potential secondary research use if an IRB conducts a limited IRB review and makes the determinations required by §46.111(a)(8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should confirm that limited IRB review has been or will be conducted when this exemption is claimed for storage/maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption Category 8 — secondary research with broad consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondary research involving identifiable private information or biospecimens is exempt if: (i) broad consent for storage/maintenance/secondary use was obtained per §46.116(a) requirements; (ii) documentation of informed consent or waiver of documentation per §46.117; (iii) an IRB conducts a limited IRB review per §46.111(a)(7) and determines the proposed research is within the scope of the broad consent; and (iv) the investigator does not include returning individual research results to subjects as part of the study plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision does not prevent compliance with legal requirements to return results. Reviewers should verify documentation of broad consent, limited IRB review, and the absence of planned individual results return when Category 8 is claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG responsibility to factor protections into overall impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) must take into account the adequacy of the proposed protections for humans, to the extent that they may be adversely affected by the project, in determining the overall impact that the research could have on the research field involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must factor their evaluation of proposed plans to protect human subjects from research risks into their overall evaluation of scientific merit and the overall impact score; inadequate protections should influence comments and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH definition of Clinical Trial
rubrics_metrics.description: A clinical trial is a research study in which one or more human subjects are prospectively assigned to one or more interventions to evaluate the effects of those interventions on health-related biomedical or behavioral outcomes. 'Prospectively assigned' refers to a pre-defined process specified in an approved protocol; 'intervention' includes manipulations of the subject or environment; 'health-related outcome' includes pre-specified goals reflecting effects on biomedical/behavioral status or quality of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply this definition to determine whether proposed work is a clinical trial and therefore whether clinical-trial-specific requirements (e.g., registration, monitoring) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-defined Phase III clinical trial
rubrics_metrics.description: A Phase III clinical trial is a broadly-based prospective Phase III clinical investigation, usually involving several hundred or more human subjects, to evaluate an experimental intervention compared with a standard/controlled intervention or compare two or more existing treatments; often aims to provide evidence for changes in health policy or standard of care and includes pharmacologic, non-pharmacologic, behavioral, community, and population-based intervention trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should recognize Phase III trials by scope and purpose; such trials generally require a DSMB and rigorous monitoring plans.
